summary: Auth system tested end-to-end. 21/24 backend pytest passed. Frontend flows all work (login gate, wrong-pw error+toast, SertexMain after login, Bearer token in axios interceptor including /api/chat 200, Settings 3-tab layout, Hesap fields visible, change-password 200 and password restored, logout clears token + returns to login). Two REAL bugs found: (1) two conversation endpoints missing auth protection, (2) brute-force lockout is bypassable in the k8s-ingress environment because request.client.host rotates between ingress pod IPs (10.49.132.77 / .78) so {ip}:{username} identifier never accumulates 3 hits.

critical.issue: Missing `user: dict = Depends(current_user)` — endpoint responds 200 with no Bearer token. server.py line ~244.
Missing `user: dict = Depends(current_user)` — endpoint responds 200 with no Bearer token. server.py line ~250. Any unauthenticated caller can delete conversations and messages.

Lockout keyed on `{request.client.host}:{username}`. In this k8s-ingress preview environment, request.client.host rotates between multiple ingress-pod IPs (observed 10.49.132.77 and 10.49.132.78). 3 rapid failed attempts distribute across 2 identifiers (e.g. .78:user count=2, .77:user count=1) — neither reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, so the 3rd attempt returns 401 instead of 429 and the lockout NEVER triggers. The single-IP happy path did trigger 429 in a previous run, confirming the mechanism works only when the IP is stable. Fix: honor X-Forwarded-For header (real client IP from the ingress) or key the lockout on username only (single-user app anyway).

minor.issue: On wrong current password, endpoint returns 401 but does NOT call _record_failure. This is fine for the change-password flow but means an authenticated attacker could brute-force the current password without triggering lockout. Consider recording failures here too.
Same as above — no lockout on wrong-current-password attempts.

ui_bugs.issue: At 1080p viewport the account tab content (curpw + newpw + newpw2 + change-password button + username change section + logout button) overflows the modal's `max-h-[60vh]` scroll region. The logout button is off-screen and requires internal scroll to reach. On smaller viewports the flow works via scroll, but the button is not immediately visible. Consider making the modal taller (e.g. max-h-[85vh]) or reordering so logout is closer to the top of the Hesap tab.

action_items: Add `user: dict = Depends(current_user)` to GET /api/conversations/{cid}/messages and DELETE /api/conversations/{cid} in server.py (both are the only routes left without the auth dep).

Fix brute-force lockout to work behind the k8s ingress: read X-Forwarded-For (first IP) as the true client IP, OR change the identifier to just `username` (this app is single-user so username-only is safe and simpler).
OPTIONAL: enlarge SettingsPanel max-height so the Hesap tab's logout button is reachable without scrolling on typical viewports (max-h-[80vh] or [85vh]).
OPTIONAL: record failed attempts on POST /api/auth/change-password and /api/auth/change-username too, to prevent an authenticated attacker from brute-forcing current_password.
CODE STYLE: logger is defined at the bottom of server.py after route handlers reference it. Works but move to top for clarity (previously flagged in iteration 1).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: routes `get_messages` and `delete_conversation` are missing the auth dependency — this is inconsistent with every other /api route and defeats the stated goal of protecting all endpoints.

auth.py `_check_lockout` / `_record_failure`: identifier includes source IP but the code uses `request.client.host` without honoring X-Forwarded-For. Behind any proxy/ingress with multiple frontends this makes the lockout ineffective (observed in this environment). For a single-user app, username-only keying is simpler and correct.

auth.py `change_password` / `change_username`: wrong-current-password path raises 401 but does not increment the failed-attempts counter. Authenticated bad actor can brute-force these without penalty.

auth.py `seed_initial_user`: if the env password is changed AFTER a UI change, the flag `password_user_set` correctly blocks override — good. But when the env password is rotated intentionally, admin has no way to force-reset without DB access. Consider a documented reset script.
SettingsPanel.jsx: modal content overflows scrollable region on Hesap tab; logout button is not initially visible on 1920x1080.
test_credentials: sertex / sertex2026 (verified working, password restored after change-password test).
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_ prefixed notes/reminders and self-clean via delete. Change-password/username tests always restore to original credentials at end. Cleaned db.login_attempts collection at end of run. Random 'lockuser_*' and 'nouser_*' identifiers used for lockout/wrong-pw tests to avoid interfering with the seeded user.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py cover auth, protection matrix, chat/tts/notes/reminders/weather with Bearer, and full change-password/change-username cycles. The 3 currently-failing tests are REAL bugs, not test issues — leave them failing until the code is fixed. Frontend flows all pass. Note: the ingress rotates client IPs so any lockout test that depends on ip-based accumulation is inherently flaky in this environment.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout ineffective: `request.client.host` returns the k8s ingress pod IP, which rotates across multiple replicas. Repro: hit /api/auth/login with wrong pw 3+ times, inspect db.login_attempts — you'll see multiple docs keyed on different {ip}:{user} pairs, each with count < MAX_ATTEMPTS. Mitigation: use `request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For', '').split(',')[0].strip()` as ip when present, else fallback to client.host — OR simply drop ip from the identifier (this is a single-user app).
